subject: Haitian Flag Day Assembly
overview: Medford High School students and administrators celebrated Haitian Flag Day through traditional dance, music, and poetry performances. The event featured the reading of a mayoral proclamation declaring May as Haitian American Heritage Month and remarks on the importance of cultural unity.

items.title: Haitian National Anthem
items.summary: Students Kernessa and Yamile performed the Haitian National Anthem to open the assembly.

items.title: Principal's Address
items.summary: Principal Paul D'Alleva discussed the history of the Haitian flag and emphasized the value of diversity within the student population.

items.title: Ibo Dance Performance
items.summary: Students performed the Ibo, a traditional dance described as a symbol of Haitian freedom and cultural core.

items.title: Superintendent's Address and Mayoral Proclamation
items.summary: Superintendent Marice Edouard-Vincent shared Haitian proverbs regarding unity and read a proclamation from Mayor Lungo-Koehn declaring May as Haitian American Heritage Month.

items.title: Student Poetry
items.summary: Students Dionysia and Wejena Prince recited original poems concerning Haitian pride, identity, and the resilience of the nation following the 2010 earthquake.

items.title: Labodai and Kompa Dance Performances
items.summary: The assembly concluded with performances of traditional Labodai and Kompa dance styles, representing Haitian cultural expression.

items.title: Closing Remarks and Recognition
items.summary: Sheryl Swalker offered closing remarks and recognized the student members and advisors of the Black Student Union for organizing the celebration.
